solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Page studied on historical period showing development of corporation

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: the Middle Ages is the medieval era of European history
to have read a subject is to have studied it

explanation.surface: A historian reads up on an era to learn how some company grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old jokey word for a paunch, so its development is a thickening waist in later life, not a business expanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation can mean a pot belly, and the growing waistline of middle years is exactly that belly developing.

clue.text: Great, I'm perplexing brilliant solver

indicators.note: perplexing means muddling up, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something great baffles even a brilliant puzzle solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional Paris police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Simenon's Paris police inspector is a famously gifted detective who cracks every case he takes on.

clue.text: Material that's dug up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: dug, as in extracted from the ground, means mined

explanation.surface: Some fabric was unearthed in an excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill cloth, a material used for jeans.

clue.text: I have way to break security device for farm animals

indicators.note: these pieces break into the device, splitting it in two

parts.note: a lock is a device that keeps a door secure
I have contracts to I've
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone forces a lock on a farm gate to get at the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock is the collective term for cattle, sheep and other animals kept on a farm.

clue.text: Article upset Italian opponent

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A newspaper article annoys an Italian rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is anti a proposal is against it, an opponent of it; the word works as a noun.

clue.text: Mufflers are incredibly soft on appropriate parts of the body

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
incredibly suggests something unbelievable done to the word are, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: P stands for piano, soft in music
lugs is informal for ears, the right parts for mufflers

explanation.surface: Mufflers feel wonderfully soft on the bits of the body they suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Earplugs deaden sound, so they muffle noise for the wearer like a silencer.

clue.text: Glue running short? Attach a staple

indicators.note: attach says the next piece is joined on after
running short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: paste is a simple glue

explanation.surface: Running out of glue, someone uses a staple instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running short' cuts the E from PASTE, leaving PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic food eaten regularly, and pasta is one in many kitchens.

clue.text: Abolish European restriction confining sodium intake at last

indicators.note: confining means holding in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a limit is a restriction
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word intake

explanation.surface: A European rule limits how much salt people may consume.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to get rid of it entirely, which is what eliminating does.

clue.text: Not working is enjoyable in period around Christmas time

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the month of Christmas
something fun is enjoyable

explanation.surface: Not being at work is pleasant over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct no longer functions or operates, so it is not working.

clue.text: New star in computing or creator of latest technology

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: IT, information technology, means computing
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A rising star of the computing world, or the inventor of a new gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who introduces new methods or devices, a pioneer of fresh technology, is an innovator.

clue.text: Vessel harboured in Murmansk if foggy

indicators.note: harboured in says the word is sheltered inside these letters, like a boat in port

explanation.surface: A boat lies sheltered in the Russian port of Murmansk when there is fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiff is a small light rowing or sailing boat, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: To send almost empty supplies is negligent

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to remit is to send, as with money

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word supplies is cleared out, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Sending almost no supplies would be careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims REMIT to REMI; 'empty' leaves SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be remiss is to be careless in one's duty, the same as being negligent.

clue.text: Assailant mauled after releasing second dog

indicators.note: mauled means savaged and pulled about, so the letters are rearranged
after releasing says one letter is let go from the word before the rest is worked

explanation.surface: An attacker savaged by a dog lets go of a second victim.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one S from ASSAILANT and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alsatian is a German shepherd, a large breed of dog often used by police.

clue.text: Additionally unpleasant smell's penetrating honk

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a toot is a honk of a horn
BO, body odour, is an unpleasant smell

explanation.surface: A nasty smell pervades, as well as a car horn's blare.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning as well, in addition, so it means additionally.

clue.text: Snake prospers with tongue half out

parts.note: a business that booms prospers

indicators.note: half out means half the word is removed, keeping the front half

parts.note: a tongue is a language

explanation.surface: A snake does well with its forked tongue half sticking out.
explanation.walkthrough: The boomslang is a venomous African tree snake; its name is Afrikaans for tree snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The boomslang is a highly venomous green tree serpent found in sub-Saharan Africa.

clue.text: I allow clothes back on in the dark

indicators.note: clothes means wraps around, so one piece covers the other

parts.note: to grant is to allow

indicators.note: back means the word on is reversed

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to put their clothes back on with the lights off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' reads as a noun in the surface but works as a verb meaning wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for knowing nothing about something, uninformed or unaware.

clue.text: Going off like a Catherine wheel?

definitions.meaning: said of milk starting to sour, beginning to spoil
a Catherine wheel is a firework that spins round as it burns

explanation.surface: A spinning firework is set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' suggests a firework igniting, but here it means turning sour. A Catherine wheel is a pinned firework that rotates while it burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Food on the point of spoiling is said to be at the turning point; a spinning firework is literally rotating.

clue.text: One never reacting to foul ingrates

indicators.note: foul suggests something fouled up, so the letters of ingrates are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm and never responds to rude, ungrateful people.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble gases such as neon and argon are chemically unreactive, hardly ever forming compounds.

clue.text: Carrying piece of hose

definitions.meaning: a shop carrying a line has it for sale
hose means leg garments, and one of a pair worn on the leg is meant

explanation.definitionFit: A shop that carries goods keeps them in supply; a nylon leg garment is a single item of hosiery.

clue.text: Large diamonds lifted in rogue's scam

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible rogue

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means turned upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: D is short for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A con man steals big diamonds as part of his fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns LD into DL, which goes inside SWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a fraudulent scheme to cheat someone out of money, a scam.

clue.text: Highlight hair on sister's head

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A sister has a highlight put in her hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' tempts as a hairdressing term, but it is a verb meaning to emphasise.
explanation.definitionFit: To highlight a point is to emphasise it, to lay weight on it.

clue.text: Start to spend pence and pounds on impulse?

definitions.text: Start to spend pence and pounds on impulse?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
start to points to the first letter of the word spend

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: Someone begins spending money freely on a whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is a spree of extravagant spending done on a whim.

clue.text: Unreliable leader in cushy job given sideways move

indicators.note: leader in points at the opening letter of the word for the job
given sideways move says that letter shifts along a place within the word

parts.note: a sinecure is a post with pay but little work

explanation.surface: An unreliable boss gets an easy post through a lateral transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sideways move' sounds like office politics, but it shifts the S of SINECURE one place to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is not firmly fixed or safe, so it cannot be relied on.

clue.text: List of works including chapter by prolific author, perhaps

parts.note: Anon, short for anonymous, is credited with so many works that it is jokingly called the most prolific author

explanation.surface: A catalogue of writings, with a chapter by a busy writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is the accepted body of works attributed to an author, a list of their genuine writings.

clue.text: Minor damage by area left of teeth

parts.note: a dent is slight damage to a surface

explanation.surface: A small mark near a patch of decay leaves some teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental is the adjective for things relating to teeth or dentistry.

clue.text: Not from the South Georgia archipelago

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the South means read upward, starting from the bottom

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: An island group that is not part of South Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South Georgia' reads as the island in the South Atlantic; the words split, 'from the South' reversing NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific kingdom made up of over 170 islands, an archipelago.

clue.text: Release setter, maybe, that's no good at all

indicators.note: no good at all means every G, the abbreviation for good, is taken out

parts.note: a setter is one breed of gundog, used in hunting

explanation.surface: A setter, perhaps a hopeless one, is let off the leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword's compiler but is the dog. Both Gs go from GUNDOG.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or a button is to unfasten it, which is to release it.

clue.text: One has raced around after daughter — it may lead to exhaustion!

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first
around means one piece goes about the other

parts.note: to have raced is to have run, giving ran
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone who has run around after their daughter would be worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it may lead to exhaustion' sounds like tiredness but suggests something being exhausted, emptied, as a pipe empties a tank; to drain is also to exhaust.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain carries water away, emptying a space, and anything draining saps energy until one is exhausted.

clue.text: Smuggler demanding an arm and a leg?

definitions.text: Smuggler demanding an arm and a leg?

parts.words: Smuggler demanding an arm and a leg?
parts.note: an arm is a gun and a leg is a run, so a smuggler of weapons who charges a fortune

explanation.surface: A smuggler charges exorbitant prices for contraband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an arm and a leg' is the idiom for a steep price, but read literally it is a weapon plus a running limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who illegally ships weapons across borders is an arms trafficker, a smuggler of firearms.

clue.text: A dash, say, to go in Geordie version of a drop scone

parts.note: say, meaning for example, is abbreviated eg
gan is the Tyneside dialect word for go; a Geordie is someone from Newcastle

indicators.note: version of says these letters are recast in a new form

explanation.surface: A sprint, perhaps, to fetch a Newcastle take on a drop scone.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England. A drop scone is a small thick pancake. The race is a school sports-day sprint carrying an egg on a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's race carrying an egg balanced on a spoon is a short sprint, a dash.
